text:
Cale Makar has one goal in his last ten games and 10 assists, which is how a two-time Norris winner ends up with a start that feels understated: 18 points in 16 games, nearly 23 minutes a night, and more lately (23.6 over the last ten). The four-assist night against Calgary on Oct. 31 did a lot of the lifting.

Underneath, nothing to worry about. He's shooting 9.1% against a range centred on 8%, and Colorado has actually scored 2.1 fewer goals than its chances with him on. The Avalanche take 57.7% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there. His top skating speed (96th percentile) and top shot (100th) haven't gone anywhere. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 2.4 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 98th percentile among defensemen, which is a forward's habit in a defenseman's minutes.

The honest caveat: Evolving-Hockey notes his teammates rank in the 99th percentile, which flatters the raw numbers. Our range: 69 to 96 points. And after Artyom Levshunov's high hit on him, Gabriel Landeskog made sure the night wasn't easy, per Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette.
headline: Makar's start is all assists, and that's fine
